title: Finite polynomial model and image identity for a tensor principal open
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $B,C$ commutative $A$-algebras. Put $D=B\otimes_A C$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(b\otimes c)(b'\otimes c')=bb'\otimes cc'$ and unit $1\otimes1$, and let $j:B\to D$ send $b$ to $b\otimes1$. For a commutative ring $H$ and $a\in H$, write $D_H(a)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(H):a\notin\mathfrak p\}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every $g\in D$ there are $n\geq0$, $b_1,\ldots,b_n\in B$, and $c_1,\ldots,c_n\in C$ with $g=\sum_i b_i\otimes c_i$ having the following properties. Set $R=A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, $S=C[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], let $\varphi_n:R\to S$ extend the structure map $A\to C$ coefficientwise, and set $h=\sum_i c_it_i\in S$. Let $e:R\to B$ be evaluation at $(b_i)$ and let $k:S\to D$ send $c\mapsto1\otimes c$ and $t_i\mapsto b_i\otimes1$. Then $k(h)=g$, $k\circ\varphi_n=j\circ e$, and the square $(R,S,B,D)$ with arrows $(\varphi_n,e,k,j)$ is a pushout of commutative rings: for every commutative ring $E$ and maps $u:S\to E$, $v:B\to E$ with $u\circ\varphi_n=v\circ e$, there is a unique ring map $w:D\to E$ with $w\circ k=u$ and $w\circ j=v$, and $w(b\otimes c)=v(b)u(c)$. Consequently the square with arrows $\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}(k)$, $\beta=\operatorname{Spec}(e)$, $q=\operatorname{Spec}(j)$ and $f_n=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_n)$ is cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product], and
$$\alpha^{-1}(D_S(h))=D_D(g),\qquad q(D_D(g))=\beta^{-1}(f_n(D_S(h))).$$
These assertions require no finiteness or flatness assumption on $B$ or $C$. Empty sums and $n=0$ are allowed.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], pure tensors generate $D$ as an $A$-module. Thus $g$ is a finite sum of scalar multiples $a_i(b_i\otimes c_i)$; absorb each scalar into $b_i$ to obtain $g=\sum_{i=1}^n b_i\otimes c_i$. This also follows directly from the free-module quotient construction in that definition. No finite generation of $B$ or $C$ is asserted.

proof.text: Write $\ell(c)=1\otimes c$. The displayed multiplication on $D$ makes $j$ and $\ell$ ring maps, and $j(a_B)=a_B\otimes1=1\otimes a_C=\ell(a_C)$ for $a\in A$ by tensor balancing [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Apply the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] to obtain $e$, the coefficient map $\varphi_n$, and $k$ with the specified coefficients and variable images. On coefficients $a\in A$ and on each $t_i$, the maps $k\varphi_n$ and $je$ agree, so they agree on $R$. Set $h=\sum_i c_it_i$. Then $k(h)=\sum_i(1\otimes c_i)(b_i\otimes1)=\sum_i b_i\otimes c_i=g$.

source.place: Tag 0F31, lemma-test-universally-open, proof of (3) implies (1), affine algebra paragraph, lines 21755--21784: finite tensor expansion, linear polynomial, specialization cartesian square and equality of images

proof.text: Fix $E,u,v$ as in the assertion, and let $u_0:C\to E$ be the restriction of $u$ to constant polynomials. Their compatibility on $A\subset R$ gives $u_0(a_C)=v(a_B)$. Give $E$ this common $A$-algebra structure. The pairing $(b,c)\mapsto v(b)u_0(c)$ is $A$-bilinear, so [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives a unique $A$-linear $w:D\to E$ with $w(b\otimes c)=v(b)u_0(c)$. It preserves the unit. On two pure tensors, multiplicativity is the equality $v(bb\prime)u_0(cc\prime)=v(b)u_0(c)v(b\prime)u_0(c\prime)$; expanding both arguments as finite sums proves it on all elements. Hence $w$ is a ring map. We have $wj=v$; on constants $wk=u_0$, and on variables $wk(t_i)=v(b_i)=u(t_i)$ by compatibility. The polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] gives $wk=u$. Any other such ring map takes $b\otimes c=j(b)\ell(c)$ to $v(b)u_0(c)$ and therefore agrees on every finite sum. This proves precisely the asserted pushout property and formula.

source.place: Tag 0F31, lemma-test-universally-open, proof of (3) implies (1), affine algebra paragraph, lines 21755--21784: finite tensor expansion, linear polynomial, specialization cartesian square and equality of images

proof.text: To pass to schemes without assuming that a topological pullback is a scheme pullback, put $T=S\otimes_R B$, where $R$ acts on $S$ by $\varphi_n$ and on $B$ by $e$. The $R$-balanced pairing $(s,b)\mapsto k(s)j(b)$ induces $F:T\to D$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The unit and multiplicativity checks are the pure-tensor calculation of step 3, now over $R$, so $F$ is a ring map. The maps $u_T:S\to T$, $s\mapsto s\otimes1$, and $v_T:B\to T$, $b\mapsto1\otimes b$, are compatible by $R$-balancing. Step 3 gives $G:D\to T$ with $Gk=u_T$ and $Gj=v_T$. The uniqueness in step 3 yields $FG=\mathrm{id}_D$. On a pure tensor $s\otimes b$, $GF(s\otimes b)=G(k(s)j(b))=(s\otimes1)(1\otimes b)=s\otimes b$, hence $GF=\mathrm{id}_T$ by generation. The affine fibre-product theorem [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], applied over $R$ to $S,B$, now identifies $\operatorname{Spec}D$ with $\operatorname{Spec}S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}B$. Since $F(s\otimes1)=k(s)$ and $F(1\otimes b)=j(b)$, its projections are exactly $\alpha,q$, and its base arrows are $f_n,\beta$.

source.place: Tags 01I4 and 01JQ, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes and lemma-fibre-product-affines; applied to the explicit mutually inverse tensor maps

proof.text: On prime ideals the induced spectrum map is contraction [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Consequently, for $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}D$, one has $\alpha(\mathfrak p)\in D_S(h)$ if and only if $h\notin k^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$, if and only if $k(h)=g\notin\mathfrak p$. Thus $\alpha^{-1}(D_S(h))=D_D(g)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image] to the cartesian square of step 4, with its $X=\operatorname{Spec}S$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $P=\operatorname{Spec}D$, $f=f_n$, $g=\beta$, $p=\alpha$, and $q=q$. For the subset $C$ of that lemma take $D_S(h)$. Its arbitrary-subset formula gives $q(\alpha^{-1}(D_S(h)))=\beta^{-1}(f_n(D_S(h)))$. Substituting step 5 proves the required image identity.

proof.text: For $g=0$ the empty expansion is permitted: take $n=0$, $R=A$, $S=C$, and $h=0$. All the constructions above still apply, and $D_S(0)$ and $D_D(0)$ are empty, so both image identities hold. Every construction used only ring operations and universal properties, which also apply to zero rings; no division, nonzero element, finiteness, or flatness hypothesis was used.
